intro: In a figure series, each figure changes from the one before by the same rule. Find the rule, then work out the next figure before you look at the options.

tips.title: Watch one thing at a time
tips.body: Follow one feature along the whole row: the number of sides, the number of dots or lines, where the shading is, which way an arrow points. Then check the next feature.

tips.title: Count sides and lines
tips.body: Many series add one each time: triangle, square, pentagon, hexagon. Some add to one part and take away from another.
tips.caption: 3, 4, 5 sides, so the next shape has 6.

tips.title: Shading and marks move round
tips.body: When a shaded part or a small mark moves, count how many parts or corners it moves each time, and which way.
tips.caption: The shading moves the same number of parts each time.

tips.title: Two rules can take turns
tips.body: Sometimes figures 1, 3, 5 follow one pattern and figures 2, 4 another: black and white in turn, lying down and standing up in turn, or a count that grows every second figure.

tips.title: Work out the answer, then find it
tips.body: Picture the next figure first, then look for it among the options. Wrong options are often the last figure again, or the right figure turned the wrong way.
